entrada.titulo: A secure and trustworthy blockchain-assisted edge computing architecture for industrial internet of things

perfil_anterior.problema: adoption of many existing models in IIoT systems with limited resources could be improved by scalability, energy consumption, and interoperability issues.
perfil_anterior.avaliacao: the proposed architecture lowers the authentication time and obtains a high response rate
perfil_anterior.possibilidades: Avaliar a integração de SSI (Self‑Sovereign Identity) para gerenciamento descentralizado de identidade nas bordas.; Implementar controle de acesso baseado em Attribute‑Based Encryption (ABE) para granularidade maior.; Comparar o consenso híbrido PoW/PoS usado em TrustChain com PBFT ou PoS em termos de latência e consumo energético.; Testar a arquitetura em múltiplas cidades inteligentes para validar interoperabilidade e escalabilidade.; Investigar conformidade com regulamentos de privacidade (ex.: GDPR) no contexto de dados industriais.

entrada.texto:
especially when it comes to effectively striking a balance between security and performance in blockchain-
based computing frameworks. Low-power IoT devices may need help to handle the high processing demands 
of blockchain consensus methods, which plague many current solutions. Furthermore, creating trust models 
that effectively manage dynamic device involvement and offer smooth interoperability across various IIoT 
platforms presents difficulties. The proposed system is employed to develop blockchain-based edge computing 
architectures suited to industrial IoT applications’ requirements.
Lightweight blockchain for resource-limited edge devices
Blockchain demands a lot of processing power for consensus techniques and sufficient space to store the whole 
blockchain when it allocates resources in edge computing. Therefore, the most critical problem in blockchain-
based resource allocation is enabling blockchain expansion in edge computing. In 39, researchers have looked 
at several ways to improve lightweight blockchains. An efficient LiTiChain blockchain is suggested in 40 to 
accommodate the edge-enabled IoT system. LiTiChain uses an End-time Ordering Graph (EOG), a tree-like 
data structure in blockchain technology, to keep track of time-sensitive activities and blocks. To save storage 
space on the edge nodes, the EOG depends on the sequence of the end time and deletes expired blocks. The 
design of EOG is adjusted to preserve the order of blocks using algorithms for k-height inclusion and deletion/
renewal of a block.
Our proposed blockchain, tailored for edge computing, is not just a theoretical concept. It is a practical 
solution that ensures fair storage and speedy, effective use of blocks. The article presents solutions for catching 
recent blocks and the best distribution of storage space for blocks41. In addition, nodes are incentivized to own 
more tokens and retain more data using an enhanced PoS consensus process tailored for edge devices with 
limited battery life. To overcome the mathematical mystery of PoW consensus, a successful consensus technique 
is suggested in42 that uses the expectation-maximization algorithm with polynomial matrix factorization as its 
basis.
Edge computing-enabled blockchain
Edge devices may support blockchain with minimal resources thanks to edge computing, a new paradigm. Put 
differently, edge computing is a facilitator of blockchain resources. A MEC-enabled blockchain architecture 
for IoT is presented in 43, wherein cloud computing resources may be purchased by IoT devices using mining 
as a service. In 44 MEC servers are separated into authentication servers (AS) and computing servers (CS) to 
reduce computing and transmission costs for vehicles with limited resources. Batch confirmation and anonymity 
techniques improve privacy and authentication effectiveness. The plan mostly depends on MEC servers’ 
dependability and accessibility, which might be problematic in areas with inadequate infrastructure or erratic 
connectivity.
Feng et al. 45 introduces PBAG, a blockchain-based authentication mechanism for the Internet of Vehicles 
(IoVs) that protects privacy. IoVs allow for real-time communication between infrastructure and automobiles, 
but they also present privacy concerns like monitoring and security risks like message forging. It uses a dynamic 
updating method supported by blockchain technology to guarantee certificate validity instead of relying on 
laborious Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs). Due to its heavy reliance on trusted authority and blockchain 
infrastructure, the protocol may be difficult to implement in rural or impoverished areas. It offers defense against 
common assaults and has been tested through simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in high-demand IoV 
scenarios. It can be challenging to balance traceability and privacy, and if the traceability mechanism is broken, 
unexpected dangers could occur. In46, two mining strategies are examined to maximize earnings for edge service 
suppliers and miners: immediate reporting following practical computing and selective reporting following 
successful computing. To increase the adaptability of blockchain, an architecture for edge computing-based 
parallel computation has been developed 47. The blockchain, acting as a decentralized database, plays a crucial 
role in synchronizing and preserving the activity information of IoT gadgets, thereby ensuring data integrity and 
security. Edge nodes are set up to carry out the parallel analyzing method by providing the verification service.
The research has provided valuable insights into the practicality of combining blockchain technology with 
edge computing for IoT applications. This knowledge, derived from studies that have used integration as a 
launchpad for applications, delves into the broad architectural challenges of integration and the intricate world 
of mitigating specific blockchain concerns. Our research has focused on developing a practical platform for 
implementing blockchain services in the IoT, with specific emphasis on meeting the recognized critical security 
and flexibility requirements for safe, decentralized storage.
The proposed blockchain enabled edge computing architecture for IIoT
The proposed structure aims to make safe handling of operations possible in intelligent industrial settings. 
These functions include initializing the system, storing data from sensors and actuators, and providing reliable 
industrial operations to clients. The following subsections give a brief description of each of these operations.
System architecture
We present a high-speed blockchain-enabled edge computing architecture tailored for medical applications. The 
proposed architecture, as depicted in Fig. 2, offers significant benefits. IoT users can efficiently dispatch tasks to 
the industry through a unified interface. The blockchain structures, which specify data dependencies, streamline 
the organization of industry tasks. The manager, leveraging the blockchain structure of operations, resource 
utilization, and network circumstances of edge servers, devises a coordination strategy.

resposta.resumo: O texto descreve desafios de dispositivos IoT de baixa potência ao executar consenso blockchain, propõe uma blockchain leve com estrutura EOG e consenso PoS aprimorado para borda, e discute a integração de computação de borda (MEC) para suportar essas soluções, apontando limitações de dependência de infraestrutura e conectividade.

Implementar controle de acesso baseado em Attribute‑Based Encryption (ABE) para granularidade maior na proteção de dados industriais.

evidencias.afirmacao: Dispositivos IoT de baixa potência têm dificuldade com as exigências de consenso blockchain.
evidencias.citacao: Low-power IoT devices may need help to handle the high processing demands of blockchain consensus methods

evidencias.afirmacao: A blockchain proposta utiliza um processo de consenso PoS aprimorado para dispositivos de borda com bateria limitada.
evidencias.citacao: enhanced PoS consensus process tailored for edge devices with limited battery life

resposta.interpretacao: O trabalho avança ao propor uma blockchain leve com estrutura de dados EOG e consenso PoS otimizado, permitindo que dispositivos de borda com recursos restritos participem de redes IIoT, embora dependa fortemente da disponibilidade de servidores MEC, o que pode limitar sua adoção em áreas com infraestrutura fraca.
resposta.duvidas: Como a solução lida com a revogação de credenciais em ambientes com conectividade intermitente? Qual o impacto real do armazenamento de blocos expirados na latência de transações? Como garantir a segurança dos nós MEC que atuam como servidores de autenticação?
